title: Is Payware Worth It? 🎬 MSFS 2024 Marketplace Explodes With New Scenery Addons!
description:
The Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 marketplace just exploded with an overwhelming wave of new content, bringing a massive mix of high-detail regional airports, historical airfields, and sprawling city overhauls. Whether you enjoy low-level helicopter operations, vintage aviation, or high-altitude airline approaches, this week covers absolutely everything.

In this comprehensive marketplace breakdown, we are putting the biggest new releases head-to-head against the default MSFS 2024 streaming engine to see which add-ons genuinely deserve a spot on your hard drive.

To make sense of this massive drop, we have organized the latest releases into four logical categories:

✈️ MODERN AIRPORTS: We kick off our walkaround on the tarmac at Nashville International (KBNA) by Dominic Design Team, featuring painstakingly handcrafted PBR pavement, dynamic night lighting, and full terminal interiors. Next, we check out Fly 2 High’s performance-optimized Birmingham Shuttlesworth (KBHM) with full GSX profile integration, followed by a dramatic alpine tour of NZA Simulations’ completely rebuilt Mount Cook Region (NZMC) featuring bespoke mountain landmark huts. We then head to Belgium to run a direct default vs. payware comparison on Brussels South Charleroi (EBCI)—testing the terminal window details and ground services against the base game—before analyzing Frankfurt Egelsbach (EDFE) by Beautiful Model of the World and Fly 2 High's Tulsa Riverside Airport (KRVS).

⏳ 1935 VINTAGE COLLECTION: Redwing takes us back in time with historically accurate overhauls of Salvador (SBSV), Natal Panamirim (SBNT), Recife Municipal (SBRF), and Victoria Airfield (SBVT), complete with vintage cars, static period aircraft, and customized era-appropriate illumination.
🏙️ GLOBAL CITYSCAPES & LANDMARKS: We explore the massive performance balance of Orbx's Landmark Singapore City Pack—including the animated Singapore cable cars and unique laser lights on the Marina Bay Sands Hotel—before diving into AC Scenery's high-fidelity Jakarta Cityscape overhaul. Plus, we check out a rapid-fire landmark dump from DFly Direct covering Montreal, New Orleans, Rio de Janeiro, and San Antonio.

💡 VFR & NIGHT ENHANCEMENTS: A deep look into the massive utility drop from Dream Scenery, separating regional industrial VFR object packs from global night lighting overhauls spanning from Liverpool to Addis Ababa.

Whether you are navigating modern airliner approaches or exploring historical grass strips, let me know in the comments below: which of these incredible packages is landing on your hard drive first?

If this marketplace breakdown helps you plan your next flight route, make sure to hit that like button and subscribe for weekly MSFS realism updates!
